headline: Margins compress y/y while earnings rebound sequentially
summary_short: Q2 FY2026 revenue fell 5.2% y/y to $7.94B (up 20.0% q/q) as a 5% drop in average home price to $371,000 outweighed a 2% rise in deliveries; net income fell 36.2% y/y to $304.8M and diluted EPS fell 31.5% y/y to $1.24, with home-sale gross margin compressing to 15.6% from 17.8%.
summary_long: Revenue fell 5.2% y/y to $7.94B as a 5% drop in average home price ($371,000) more than offset a 2% rise in deliveries (20,519 homes) amid continued market weakness and still-elevated incentives (12.9% of revenue). Home-sale gross margin fell to 15.6% from 17.8% on lower revenue per square foot and higher land costs, partly offset by lower construction costs. Net income fell 36.2% y/y to $304.8M ($1.24 diluted EPS, $1.31 ex a $23.3M tech-investment mark-to-market loss). Homebuilding cash fell to $1.82B from $3.44B on H1 buybacks and land spend. For Q3, Lennar guides to 20,500-21,500 deliveries and ~16% gross margin, and trimmed full-year delivery guidance to 82,000-83,000 homes.

drivers.explanation: Home sales revenue fell 2% y/y as a 5% drop in average sales price ($371,000 vs $389,000) was only partly offset by a 2% rise in deliveries (20,519 homes); price weakness reflects continued market softness.
Home-sale gross margin fell to 15.6% from 17.8% on lower revenue per square foot and higher land costs year over year, partly offset by lower construction costs from cost-saving initiatives.

Homebuilding operating earnings fell as gross margin compressed and SG&A rose to 9.2% of home-sale revenue from 8.8% on lower revenue leverage and higher marketing/selling spend; Financial Services operating earnings also fell on lower profit per locked loan.

Net income fell mainly on lower Homebuilding gross margin, a higher SG&A ratio, and a smaller Financial Services contribution, partly offset by a narrower technology-investment mark-to-market loss ($23.3M vs $29.4M) than a year ago.
EPS fell in step with lower net income; diluted share count also fell 7.5% y/y on continued buybacks, which cushioned the per-share decline relative to the net income decline.
Share count fell as the company repurchased $446.7M of stock in Q2 (4.3M Class A + 0.7M Class B shares) under its ongoing buyback program, which had $1.0B of remaining authorization at quarter-end.

Management describes Q2 as strong execution against a tougher macro backdrop (elevated mortgage rates, rising inflation) but cites a 'meaningful decline' in sales incentives this quarter as a possible early margin-recovery signal; guides Q3 to 20,500-21,500 deliveries and ~16% gross margin, and trimmed FY delivery guidance to 82,000-83,000 homes.
